title: [poll] Which of the four verdicts is most common in your system?
body:
> **Calibration poll.** Guess, then go and measure, then reply with what you actually found.

Every failed answer is one of four things — see [The Four Verdicts](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/60-cheatsheets/frameworks/four-verdicts.md):

- **A** — **Retrieval miss.** The evidence was never in the candidate pool
- **B** — **Packing loss.** It was in the pool and did not survive into the prompt
- **C** — **Generation failure.** It was in the prompt and the answer was still wrong
- **D** — **Right by accident.** The answer was right and the evidence was never retrieved

### The interesting part

On this repository's corpus the split was **84 packing loss against 27 retrieval miss** — the
bottleneck was three-to-one on the stage nobody was working on.

Most people guess A. Most people are wrong, and they are wrong in a direction that costs a month
of encoder work on a problem that was `k=8`.
---

**How to vote.** The API cannot create a native poll widget, so vote with a reaction on this post — 👍 A · 🎉 B · 😄 C · 🚀 D — and reply if your answer needs a condition attached. The reveal is posted as a **reply** in about a week, never by editing this body: editing would destroy the record of what you were actually asked.
